newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end firmer, wipe out earlier losses.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end firmer, wipe out earlier losses.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks reversed earlier losses to close firmer on Friday ahead of Monday's federal election. * 10 of 14 sub-indices ended higher. * 92 million shares traded worth C$1.7 billion.
Toronto stocks reversed earlier losses on Friday to end on a firmer note, helped by stronger bonds after investors decided the key index had sold off enough in recent sessions.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index closed 11.79 points higher at 6382.12, aided by a rally in North American bond markets, said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn's director of private client investing.
The index dropped more than 50 points at the open after investors were spooked by a forecast of disappointing second quarter results from computer chip maker Intel Corp.
However, Toronto turned around as bonds rallied on signs of subdued inflation from U.S. economic figures and gains in the Canadian currency.
"A very, very impressive reversal," Best said. "There had been a couple days' sell-off and there had been fill-in" as investors returned to snap up issues.
Canada's largest equities market lost ground for most of the week after setting record highs on Monday. The weekly losses totaled 57 points from Monday's open of 6441 points.
Investors are eyeing Monday's federal election in Canada, however a Liberal Party majority seemed assured according to recent polls, Best said.

Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-groups closed in positive territory, led by media, conglomerates, consumer products and banks. The weaker side included golds, utilities, forestry products and industrial products.
Advancing issues outpaced decliners 550 to 438 while 286 ended steady.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc., Canada's largest publicly traded firm, slipped 0.30 to 36.35.
Heavyweight BCE topped most actives and pulled the rest of the market south.
* Transportation firm Bombardier Inc rose 0.25 to 29.00 after Friday's news that Comair Inc said it signed a firm order for 18 aircraft worth $330 million.
